data.title: Brightline Interactive Faces Nasdaq Delisting, Plans Appeal
data.description:
An announcement from Brightline Interactive Inc ( (BTLN) ) is now available.

On September 11, 2026, Brightline Interactive, Inc. disclosed that it had received a Nasdaq staff determination to delist its common stock for failing to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement. The deficiency arose after the stock closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days beginning March 13, 2026, and the company did not regain compliance by the September 9, 2026 deadline, triggering the delisting process and raising concerns about future liquidity and investor access.

Brightline Interactive plans to appeal the Nasdaq decision by requesting a hearing before a Nasdaq Hearings Panel, a step that temporarily stays any suspension of trading and related regulatory filings. The company’s shares will remain listed on Nasdaq pending the panel’s written decision, but there is no assurance the appeal will succeed or that Brightline will be able to meet listing criteria within any additional period that might be granted, leaving shareholders facing continued uncertainty over the stock’s exchange status.

data.title: NET Power Restructures Oxy-Combustion Partnership With Baker Hughes
data.description:
The latest update is out from NET Power ( (NPWR) ).

On September 8, 2026, NET Power and Baker Hughes affiliates executed a set of integrated agreements that indefinitely suspend their joint development and commercialization programs for utility-scale oxy-combustion power plants while amending an existing license for industrial-scale applications. The move stems from changing market and economic conditions and NET Power’s conclusion that continuing the specific utility-scale turboexpander and platform programs is not currently economical.

Under the new arrangements, performance under the Amended and Restated Joint Development Agreement and the Commercial Agreement is frozen for an indefinite period, and Baker Hughes’ special access and exclusivity rights over NET Power’s La Porte, Texas demonstration facility are terminated. At the same time, Baker Hughes’ Nuovo Pignone affiliates retain exclusive rights to utility-scale equipment packages and gain revised, largely royalty-based industrial licensing terms, though no party is obligated to deploy plants and no royalty amounts are set or assured.
